title: Client-controlled basket cookie is deserialized with pickle
description: The basket cookie is entirely controlled by the client, but it is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code in the server process when any basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: read_basket() obtains request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)) without a signature or integrity check.

title: Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-supplied tokens
description: The refresh endpoint disables JWT signature verification, then trusts the token's sub claim to select the user. An attacker can submit an unsigned token naming any user and receive a freshly signed token for that account.
evidence: jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}) is used before load_user(claims.get('sub')) and make_token(user).

title: Authentication decorator swallows 401 errors and continues execution
description: require_auth catches the HTTPException raised by abort(401), clears g.user, and still calls the protected handler. This makes authentication fail open; for example, the gift-card balance handler returns card balances without a token.
evidence: The except Exception block catches abort(401) at line 54 and then returns f(*args, **kwargs) at line 58; balance() only queries the requested card and does not require g.user.

title: Authenticated users can view any order by ID
description: The order detail endpoint authenticates the caller but calls get_order directly, which filters only by order ID and never checks customer_id. Any signed-in customer can read another customer's order status, items, payment totals, and refunds by changing the ID.
evidence: show_order() returns order_json(get_order(order_id)); unlike own_order(), get_order() has no comparison with g.user['id'].

title: Trailing slash bypasses the admin authorization hook
description: The global admin check compares request.path to a set containing only the canonical route strings. The refunds route accepts a trailing slash, so /admin/refunds/ is dispatched without the staff check and permits unauthenticated refunds.
evidence: staff_only_admin checks request.path in admin_paths, while the route is declared strict_slashes=False. A POST to /admin/refunds/ was accepted with HTTP 200 and created a refund without Authorization.

title: Product search concatenates the query directly into SQL
description: The public search endpoint inserts q directly into a SQL statement. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and use SQLite expression/UNION injection to disclose data or cause database errors.
evidence: The query is built as "... name LIKE '%" + q + "%' OR sku LIKE '%" + q + "%' ..." instead of using bound parameters.

title: Staff review report is vulnerable to SQL injection through display names
description: A customer's display_name is interpolated into the review-report SQL. A customer can set a display name containing SQL syntax, after which a staff member viewing that customer's report executes the injected query.
evidence: The report uses f"WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ORDER BY r.id DESC" with no parameter binding.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review text, and product pages render it with the safe filter. A malicious review can execute JavaScript in every visitor's browser in the shop origin.
evidence: add_review() stores body without HTML sanitization, while the template renders r.body with {{ r.body|safe }}.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: User passwords are hashed with unsalted SHA-256, which is designed for speed rather than password storage. A database disclosure therefore enables efficient offline cracking and reuse of recovered credentials.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() and stores that value directly as password_hash.

title: Payment status timeouts are treated as successful payments
description: If the payment provider times out, the checkout endpoint sets the order to processing and paid_pence to the full total. A timeout is not proof of settlement, so an order can be fulfilled without a confirmed payment.
evidence: The requests.Timeout handler sets status = 'paid', followed by UPDATE orders SET status = 'processing', paid_pence = total_pence.

title: JWT signing key is hardcoded in source
description: The application uses a fixed source-controlled SECRET_KEY for HS256 JWTs. Anyone who obtains the repository or a deployed copy can forge authentication tokens, including staff tokens.
evidence: SECRET_KEY is assigned the literal value "hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d" rather than being required from a protected deployment secret.

title: Payment webhook signature does not authenticate event contents
description: The webhook MAC covers only order_id, while status and amount_pence are accepted from the unsigned JSON body. Anyone able to obtain the webhook secret can change a valid signed event into an arbitrary payment amount or status. The configured fallback secret is also a fixed value.
evidence: webhook_signature() hashes only str(order_id), but payment_webhook() trusts event['status'] and event['amount_pence']; WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to 'whsec-local' in config.py line 8.
